message.content:
In Christian theology, the figure most often regarded as the central “prophetic” voice is **Jesus Christ**. While Jesus is not a prophet in the same way that Moses or Isaiah were, Christians believe that He is the fulfillment of all Old‑Testament prophecy and the ultimate revelation of God’s will. Because of this, He is usually considered the most important prophetic figure in Christianity.

Other prophets are also highly significant:

| Prophet | Role in Christian tradition |
|---------|-----------------------------|
| **Moses** | Delivered the Law (the Torah) and led Israel out of Egypt; his story is foundational for Christian understanding of covenant and redemption. |
| **Isaiah** | Prophesied the coming of the Messiah; many of his passages are quoted in the New Testament. |
| **John the Baptist** | Prepares the way for Jesus, calling people to repentance; he is often called the “last prophet” because he heralds the arrival of Christ. |

So, while many Christians honor the prophets of the Hebrew Bible, Jesus Christ is typically viewed as the most pivotal prophetic figure in Christianity.
